subject: Fleet rightsizing worksheet & latency/traffic profile for HorizonAI deal
messages:
From: Erica Yang <erica@horizonai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tom@horizonai.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity—initial traffic snapshot and ask

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this with HorizonAI. We’re moving toward a committed reserved fleet for Q1 and want to get a realistic sizing estimate before the pricing/commitment conversation. High-level: production LLM assist across our dev tools (short prompts) + a nightly batch embedding job for search reindexing.

Quick numbers from our telemetry (rough):
- Typical QPS (steady): 45 req/s
- Peak QPS (5–10 min bursts): 420 req/s
- Avg prompt length: 35 tokens
- Avg model response: 180 tokens (higher for some flows)
- Interactive sessions: ~25k daily active sessions with session affinity (KV cache used)
- Embedding batch: 150M texts nightly (windowed)

We’d like your fleet-sizing worksheet (tokenized traffic, concurrency mapping, burst assumptions) and a short checklist of tradeoffs for p50/p95/p99 latency targets. Can you send a template we can fill and a short list of clarifying questions?

Erica
Erica Yang
Head of Infrastructure, HorizonAI
erica@horizonai.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Erica Yang <erica@horizonai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity—initial traffic snapshot and ask

Thanks Erica — sending the worksheet attached (fleet-rightsizing-template-v2.xlsx). I populated a few baseline assumptions from your note, but we’ll want to confirm the items below so sizing reflects your production realities:

1) Prompt/response distribution: is 35/180 tokens the median or mean? Do you have a prompt-length histogram (percentiles)?
2) Burst shape: how often do 5–10 min peaks occur (daily, weekly)? Are there calendar-driven peaks (e.g., product launches)?
3) Session affinity: is KV cache mandatory for correctness (stateful) or just a perf optimization? If mandatory, what fraction of requests need a hot KV hit?
4) Embedding ingest: confirm nightly window (hours), concurrency, and whether we can offload to CPU-only instances for batching/throughput.
5) Latency SLOs: target p50/p95/p99 and what you consider acceptable fallback behavior during overloads (queueing vs. graceful degradation).

Internal note: CC’ing Aditya and Karthik to propose a conservative capacity baseline from these numbers and identify where quantization/caching can reduce GPU footprint. Marissa, can you flag any upcoming pricing/commitment deadlines with Horizon?

If you prefer, we can run a 60-minute sizing workshop — I’ve included a draft agenda in the worksheet. Next steps: you can fill the highlighted cells or send sample telemetry and we’ll run the initial carve.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: fleet-rightsizing-template-v2.xlsx (worksheet with token buckets, burst shape slider, session affinity toggles)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Erica Yang <erica@horizonai.com>
Date: 2025-10-14T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity—initial traffic snapshot and ask

Mina — quick baseline assumptions I’d propose while we wait for sample telemetry:
- Baseline concurrency target for steady 45 req/s: assume 10 concurrent in-flight tokens per GPU (conservative), map to ~0.5 GPU steady if using T4-class or 0.6 NV6-class equivalence.
- For 420 req/s 10-minute burst: treat as sustained 5–10k token/s injection; plan for autoscale headroom of 6–8x baseline if enabling burst routing to reserved pool.
- Latency goals: if Horizon wants p95 < 250ms for interactive routes, we’ll need lower batch sizes and larger fleet; p99 < 600ms is often feasible with small cache hits and prefetching.

Questions for sizing worksheet (to add):
A) Which model family (e.g., Llama-2-70B vs smaller open LLM)? Smaller models change GPU mix significantly.
B) Do you run any synchronous tool-calling or complex IO per request?
C) Are there throughput constraints on upstream systems that would naturally gate bursts?

I’ll draft a conservative GPU mix in the worksheet and mark where quantization vs KV caching reduces unit cost.

—Aditya
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Becker <tom@horizonai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Erica Yang <erica@horizonai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity—initial traffic snapshot and ask

Mina / team — answers inline below and attaching a short sample of production telemetry (sample_telemetry.csv) for the last 7 days.

1) Prompt/response distribution: the 35 token prompt is median; mean is ~48 tokens. The response distribution is skewed — median 150 tokens, mean ~210 tokens. We’ll attach a histogram later.
2) Burst cadence: peaks happen ~2–3x per week tied to customer reports and external triggers; two large spikes last month (marketing demos).
3) KV cache: session affinity is required for certain UX flows (about 60% of interactive requests expect a warm KV). Fallback to cold-start is acceptable but increases latency and token cost.
4) Embedding window: nightly 3AM–7AM UTC, we prefer GPU-accelerated batch for throughput but can evaluate CPU/GPU hybrid. Batch concurrency limited by our uploader at ~1k parallel multipart jobs.
5) SLOs: target p50 100–120ms, p95 240–300ms for core assist routes; p99 target is soft (we can accept up to 800ms during bursts but want mitigation strategies).

Attachment: sample_telemetry.csv (7-day rolling token counts, QPS by endpoint, session hit-rates).

Thanks — Tom

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Erica Yang <erica@horizonai.com>, Tom Becker <tom@horizonai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-16T15:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity—initial traffic snapshot and ask

Tom / Erica — great, thanks for the telemetry sample. Next steps and proposed workshop:

1) We’ll ingest the CSV and run a tokenized traffic carve to produce two capacity options: (A) conservative reserved fleet to meet p95/p50 targets with <10% overflow risk, and (B) optimized fleet that leans on quantization + aggressive KV caching to lower committed GPU count (with slightly higher p99 risk during rare spikes).
2) Proposed 60-minute workshop (remote): agenda = review telemetry, confirm model family & quantization levers, run a quick cost/latency simulation, and align on commitment window.
3) I attached the worksheet with the cells we filled and the draft agenda. Also including a DocuSign link for a mutual NDA (if you want it signed before we pull longer-term telemetry).

Proposed times (PST): Tue 10/21 10:00–11:00, Wed 10/22 14:00–15:00. Please confirm what works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: fleet-rightsizing-template-v2.xlsx (worksheet), sample_telemetry.csv (7-day sample)
